# 0. Optimus AI Gateway architecture
The Gateway is a deterministic strict-loopback process. Agent-facing configuration remains only OPTIMUS_GATEWAY_URL and OPTIMUS_API_KEY. The Gateway holds the approved developer aggregator credential in its own local environment or OS credential storage. With durable accounting configured, it alone resolves the Postgres credential from its Gateway-owned keyring namespace; the host uses only its existing Gateway URL and key (§13.13). No hosted Optimus service, OAuth/device flow, tenant wallet, Vault or public origin is introduced.
OpenRouter remains the default aggregator. Vercel is an optional second OpenAI-compatible endpoint by design; no Vercel integration exists at 91fd64a. Direct provider adapters remain removed.
:::flow
Local Optimus agent - URL/shared secret only
Authenticated loopback Gateway at 127.0.0.1:8765
Trusted policy + domains + finite calls + complete request capacity
Independent adapters -> approved upstream / public tools / OTLP
Provider-reported usage -> host settlement -> durable outbox -> Gateway-owned Postgres
:::end
| Ingress / adapter | Downstream responsibility |
|---|---|
| /v1/responses; /v1/chat/completions | One approved OpenAI-compatible model transport; preserve distinct input/messages shapes |
| /v1/tools/web/search | Separate authorized search request. Tavily-backed at 91fd64a (Gateway-only `TAVILY_API_KEY`); the deterministic aggregator-plugin contract in §9C.1 is the target |
| /v1/tools/web/extract | Bounded HTTPS extract with provenance and revalidation |
| /v1/tools/package/lookup | Public PyPI/npm/Maven clients; construction independent of Tavily/search configuration under #361, with Redis URL and domain policy required |
| /v1/tools/security/advisory | Public OSV client; same implemented metadata independence and required Redis/domain safeguards as package lookup |
| /v1/observability/traces | Structured trace validation/redaction -> OTel/OTLP -> Phoenix by default |
| /v1/decisions | Typed Auto classifier decision; original contract in §13.10.4 |
| /v1/observability/usage-capture | Host outbox upload -> Gateway-owned Postgres transaction and committed acknowledgement (§13.13) |
| /v1/observability/usage-report | Capabilities or bounded read-only session/turn report; no model call (§13.14) |
All ten listed routes are POST routes and authenticate locally at `a88fde8`. No MCP endpoint is added. Product dollar stops remain removed under the accepted migration; independent evaluation ceilings retain their own authority.

| External component | Preserved edge |
|---|---|
| OpenRouter | Approved default model transport; separately authorized search is a target |
| Tavily | Implemented web-search provider at 91fd64a; Gateway-only key; replacement pending |
| Vercel | Design option; no integration at the inspected source |
| PyPI / npm / Maven | Independent package APIs |
| OSV | Independent advisory API |
| Phoenix / OTLP collector | Sanitized configured trace export |
| Redis / RedisTimeSeries | Existing agent state and telemetry; not the durable report ledger |
| Postgres | Optimus-owned durable capture/report ledger; credential resolved only by the Gateway |
The host owns Agent planning count/time/failure bounds; the Gateway owns enabled trusted request policy and capacity.

# C. Gateway responsibilities

- Authenticate the local agent with a shared secret on strict loopback.
- Resolve model aliases through an approved OpenAI-compatible aggregator.
- Broker web search and extract through the configured web provider; package lookup and OSV advisory are independently constructed and served without a Tavily key under #361. Redis/domain prerequisites remain shared. Separate extract-backend independence and the search-path decision remain unimplemented targets owned by #362.
- Enforce execution mode, tool policy, domain rules, call caps, provenance, complete request capacity and finite work.
- Persist run/session/request/Gateway/provider request attribution.
- Isolate upstream credentials and the Gateway-owned Postgres credential from the agent process.
- Accept structured trace ingress, map it to OTel, and export OTLP.

```text

POST /v1/responses
```

All routes authenticate with the local shared secret. Trace ingress is operational, not a

# 0A. Local vs. Gateway Configuration and Provider-Cost Mapping

## Phase 1 runtime rule

The agent runtime allows only `OPTIMUS_GATEWAY_URL` and `OPTIMUS_API_KEY`. The Gateway owns the
developer's approved aggregator credential. Local agent-side Tavily, OpenAI, OpenRouter, GLM,
LangSmith, or other provider keys are rejected.

## Provider-cost mapping

`OPTIMUS_API_KEY` is a local shared secret, not a wallet key. The developer funds the aggregator
account directly. The Gateway returns normalized provider-reported usage. At `a88fde8`, the host accepts receipts through `TurnSettlement`; durable capture drains from its local outbox through the Gateway into an Optimus-owned Postgres ledger (§13.13). Redis telemetry is separate.

The carried "Gateway Tool and Observability Endpoints" page that follows is historical: its seven-route listing is not exhaustive at `a88fde8`. The current ten-route inventory is in §0 and §D, including decisions, usage capture and usage report. This qualification preserves the native page without presenting its incomplete list as the current API.

| Call class | Required accounting |
|---|---|
| Model completion | aggregator, actual provider/model when returned, tokens/cache, billing units, provider-reported `cost_usd`, request IDs |
| Web search | Tavily provider at 91fd64a: provider-native `tavily_credits` units recorded as `ProviderUsage` with request identity; the deterministic aggregator plugin (separate minimal model call, structured citations, search-use accounting) is the target |
| Package/advisory | operational request evidence; no fabricated provider cost |
| Trace export | delivery state and trace IDs; no allocated/amortized request charge |
| Usage-report read | existing canonical ledger facts and explicitly labelled estimates; no model dispatch or new provider charge |

```text
Agent shared secret
  -> loopback Gateway trust, capacity and accounting
  -> developer aggregator account
  -> provider-reported usage and USD cost
  -> GatewayUsage + host receipt settlement
  -> local durable outbox -> authenticated Gateway capture -> Postgres ledger
```

The USD rename is complete at 91fd64a: ACP result payloads carry `ledger_run_total_cost_usd` and
`ledger_run_total_billing_units` (`optimus/acp/dispatcher.py`), and no credit-named ledger field remains under
`src/`. The rename changed no USD semantics and introduced no cross-run policy.

# 6. Resilient Aggregator Calling Layer and Tenacity Rules

All model completions route from the agent to the strict-loopback Gateway using the local shared
secret. The Gateway resolves an Optimus model alias to an aggregator model identifier and calls
the approved OpenAI-compatible upstream: OpenRouter by default (Vercel AI Gateway is a design option with no integration at 91fd64a).

The aggregator credential exists only in Gateway-owned local configuration or OS credential
storage. There is no Vault, hosted Optimus account, or direct single-provider adapter.

## Two agent-facing shapes, one upstream transport

- `/v1/responses` accepts the Responses API `input` field.
- `/v1/chat/completions` accepts the Chat Completions `messages` array.
- The validator rejects `messages` at `/v1/responses` and `input` at
  `/v1/chat/completions`.
- Both paths converge on one authenticated completion service.
- The surviving transport is `UrllibOpenAICompatibleClient` in
  `src/optimus_gateway/upstream_client.py` (built by `optimus_gateway.providers.build_upstream_client`).

The legacy host permits an initial attempt plus at most three retries (`optimus/retry/policy.py`, `max_retries = 3`; the enforced-policy limit is `MAX_ROUTE_ATTEMPTS = 2` in `optimus_model_policy/binding.py`). The inactive-policy Gateway separately permits at most three upstream attempts, including its legacy transient timeout/URL/5xx retries. Once enforcement is active, the Gateway permits one primary attempt and at most one identical-payload resend on the same route, only after a definitely NOT_SENT result (including a proven pre-connection timeout) or rejected HTTP 429. A timeout after connection, uncertain delivery, 5xx or unknown accounting is not resent. The host honors non-retryable classifications so it cannot multiply attempts. This resend policy adds no alternative-model recovery. ADR-029's single later recovery move is a separate interactive Auto planning action (§13.11), not a resend of an uncertain or failed provider attempt. The per-request timing budget is specified in §13.12. Each physical attempt retains its own receipt.

Provider-reported `usage.cost` is authoritative in the corrected architecture. Missing, null,
negative, or malformed usage/cost fails closed before generated output is accepted.

# 6.1 OpenAI-compatible upstream pattern

```python
class UrllibOpenAICompatibleClient:
    """Gateway-owned aggregator transport.

    The agent never receives the upstream URL or credential. The transport
    has no direct-provider selection branch.
    """

    def __init__(self, *, api_key: str, base_url: str) -> None:
        self._api_key = api_key
        self._base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")

    def create_message(
        self, *, model: str, input_text: str
    ) -> ProviderMessageResult:
        payload = {
            "model": model,
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": input_text}],
        }
        body = self._post_json("/chat/completions", payload)
        return parse_openai_compatible_message_and_usage(body)
```

`parse_openai_compatible_message_and_usage` must validate output, provider request identity,
billing units, token/cache detail, resolved model/version when present, and provider-reported USD
cost. The Gateway returns the requested agent-facing shape plus the same validated GatewayUsage
contract.

```text
Agent /v1/responses "input" --------\
                                      > completion service
Agent /v1/chat/completions "messages"/       |
                                             v
                         OpenAI-compatible aggregator transport
```

The upstream transport may use Chat Completions while the Gateway preserves both agent-facing
contracts. Those shapes must never be mixed.

# 9D. Gateway Server-Side Policy Revalidation

The Gateway independently revalidates every privileged input. Agent-side checks are defense in
depth and never authoritative.

| Control | Gateway enforcement |
|---|---|
| Allowed domains | Intersect caller request with local allowlist; forward effective policy; reject returned URLs outside it |
| Extract provenance | Require exact prior search result for the same `run_id`; revalidate redirects and final URL |
| Capacity and accounting | Enforce the complete request guard under trusted policy; retain actual usage and explicit unknowns. Product monetary stops are removed only by the released Task 11 migration. Evaluation spend limits are separately scoped. |
| Call caps | Key by run and tool; do not share a paid-search configuration gate |
| Tool policy | Recheck tool class, policy signal, execution mode, and authenticated local subject |
| Usage | Reject missing, malformed, negative, or unparseable provider-reported cost |

```python
def authorize_tool_call(request, *, policy, ledger):
    effective_domains = policy.intersect_domains(request.domains)
    policy.require_tool_allowed(request.tool, request.execution_mode)
    policy.require_call_capacity(request.run_id, request.tool)
    require_final_capacity_and_output(request, policy)
    return AuthorizedToolCall(
        request=request,
        effective_domains=effective_domains,
    )
```

There is no org/project dimension. Cross-run spend policy remains `P9.85-FU-3` and is not added by
this correction.

# 10. Usage Accounting Service and TimeSeries Policy

`UsageAccountingService` accepts only validated GatewayUsage/ProviderUsage records. It persists
provider-reported billing units, tokens/cache details, model/version, and `cost_usd`.

```python
# Illustrative shape. The implemented method is UsageAccountingService.record_gateway_usage
# in src/optimus/usage/accounting.py; it enforces the same validation before appending.
def record_usage(self, usage: GatewayUsage, *, context: RequestContext) -> None:
    require_nonempty(usage.gateway_request_id)
    require_nonnegative_decimal(usage.cost_usd)
    require_nonnegative_int(usage.billing_units)
    self.ledger.append(
        ProviderUsage.from_gateway_usage(usage, context=context)
    )
```

It never substitutes a locally calculated charge when provider cost exists. Missing, null,
negative, or malformed cost fails closed before generated content or evidence is applied.

A versioned price snapshot may remain as labeled diagnostic/comparison metadata only. It cannot
overwrite provider-reported cost or silently supply a release-grade value.

**Production qualification at a88fde8.** The preceding `UsageAccountingService` listing is a retained component contract, not the production ACP settlement wiring. Production uses host `TurnSettlement`, extended by durable capture and Gateway-owned Postgres delivery (§13.13). The Redis settled-usage sink is not wired into that production settlement path. Existing Redis agent state and telemetry remain.

This qualification also applies to the carried §10.1/§10A material that follows: its RedisTimeSeries implementation and historical policy do not identify the durable ledger read by the savings report. Provider-reported charges remain authoritative. Registry snapshots preserve actual-side provenance; independent dated reference snapshots support B1 estimates only (§13.16), never replacement settled charges.

## Required identity

- `run_id`
- `session_id`
- `request_id`
- `gateway_request_id`
- `provider_request_id` when returned
- aggregator and actual provider when returned
- requested alias and resolved model/version

# 12. Guardrail and Workflow Component Contracts

All model-touching guardrails use the same loopback Gateway, developer aggregator account, actual accounting and explicit evaluation caps, provider-reported cost, and OTel trace path.

This section specifies the Phase 1 enforcement and workflow components introduced as a cross-cutting
concern in HLD §13. The authoritative policy rationale lives in the companion Agent Execution
Guardrails & Workflow Strategy v1.4 (§2-§9); the representative Pydantic type shapes are in its
§10.2. The contracts below are owned by this section. All model-touching elements (the borderline
classifier and the loop completion evaluator) route through the Optimus Gateway under the existing
developer aggregator account and normalized ledger (§0A, §10A); the guardrails introduce no second
cost path.

## 12A. Permission & Pre-Tool Enforcement

PermissionPolicy evaluates mode -> user_deny -> project_allow -> impact -> classifier and returns
a single PermissionDecision (ALLOW | DENY | HOLD); deny always precedes allow; the
classifier cannot overturn a deny.

PermissionDecision contains verdict, layer, rule_id, reason, and
requires_human_approval.

PreToolGuard fires after the agent assembles a tool call, before execution (cf. PreToolUse), for
every tool class (bash, file_edit, mcp_call, web); deterministic checks run before any classifier.
It returns PreToolResult.

CommandSafetyValidator is a local, in-process shell validator covering destructive commands,
pipe-to-shell, environment/credential access, Unicode homoglyph/confusable characters, ANSI/control
sequences, insecure transport, and unexpected network egress. Satisfiable by Tirith or an equivalent
validator; the design takes no hard dependency on any one implementation. Implemented in-process in
`optimus/guardrails/command_safety.py` at 91fd64a; Tirith is not a dependency.

ToolInvocationAuditEvent is an append-only record of each decision (verdict, layer, failed checks,
approver) feeding the same trace sink as evidence and cost telemetry.

## 12B. Prompt-Injection & MCP Supply-Chain Trust

MCPTrustRegistry captures server_id, manifest_hash, allowed_tools, permission_scope, and
approved. MCP servers are never auto-loaded from cloned repositories; a manifest-hash change
forces re-approval; tool descriptors (name/description/schema) are inspected for injection before
being surfaced to the planner.

ConfigTrustScanner treats agent config and rule files as code, scanning on ingest for embedded
instructions, exfiltration endpoints, and homoglyph/ANSI content before they may influence behavior.

## 12C. Bounded Agent Loops

GoalLoopController, IterationState, CompletionEvaluator, ProgressLedger,
LoopBudgetPolicy (max_iterations, max_wall_clock_minutes, repeated_failure_limit; `max_budget_usd` defaults to None and is set only by an explicitly capped evaluation caller; the model default for repeated_failure_limit is 3 in `optimus/loops/models.py` and ACP planning composes 2), and
LoopStopReason (COMPLETED | MAX_ITERATIONS | WALL_CLOCK | REPEATED_FAILURE | HUMAN_HALT; BUDGET_EXHAUSTED only for independent evaluation) are the bounded-loop contracts.

Persistent state lives in files, git history, task manifests, traces, and the evidence ledger (§9E),
not in an ever-growing chat context. The pre-tool guard (§12A) is never bypassed inside a loop, and
the completion evaluator is a reserved cheap Gateway-routed capability. This section does not claim it is active; unknown costs do not latch a product goal loop. Task 11 removes the product monetary predicates on the reviewed cf9bb9d branch. Independent evaluation monetary policy remains explicit.

# 4. Scope classification and strategy selection (continued)
The following retained prototype illustrates scope classification; it is not a new runtime activation or additional policy decision. Ordered branches:
| Priority | Condition | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Shared module touched; multiple directory roots; structural create/delete across more than one file; or more than three files | MULTI_FILE_CHANGESET |
| 2 | Structural create/delete; or one file with more than 100 lines | FILE_MUTATION |
| 3 | More than 15 lines | PATCH_PROPOSAL |
| 4 | Otherwise | INLINE_SNIPPET |
Execution strategy remains harness-controlled. Start with at most five tool calls and zero reflection passes; a validation failure or shared-module change selects bounded Reflection with at most 15 calls and three passes. High task risk or a multi-file changeset selects Plan-and-Execute with at most ten calls and one reflection. High ambiguity otherwise selects ReAct with at most 12 calls. Other work uses Direct execution. No new mandatory reflection loop is introduced.
At `bf440cb`, trusted registry enforcement is active. Ordinary launches use a configured eligible fixed model; approved Auto launches classify and bind a planning/answer model per turn (§13.10). Both obey final complete-request capacity, with a planning/answer ceiling of 262144 including one output reserve and the admitted route's smaller bounds where applicable. Explicit empirical admission does not establish a universal token bound. Retire the old branch-specific 100000/150000/250000 token ceilings and HAIKU/PRO aliases. History strategy allocations and final packing remain separate. These retained scope/strategy prototypes do not implement H or determine its task tier. At `5977155`, ADR-029 permits one mid-turn recovery escalation in interactive Auto planning (§13.11); approved application uses the moved-to model. This is the bounded exception to Auto's turn binding.
Mutation enforcement continues in section 4: PLAN cannot perform WRITE or EXTERNAL_MUTATION and raises the typed validation error. The existing MutationGuard wraps that assertion before execution; the continuation on the next page retains its path-containment contracts.

# 4A. Valid and invalid transitions
Every transition is deterministic; model text cannot override a rejection. Existing mode and exact-approval checks remain required.
| From | To | Permitted / condition |
|---|---|---|
| Idle | Planning | Yes, user request |
| Planning | PlanReady | Yes, requirements and mode resolved |
| PlanReady | ChatOnly | Yes, Plan/Chat; no mutation |
| PlanReady | Executing directly | No; AwaitingApproval cannot be bypassed |
| PlanReady | AwaitingApproval | Yes, Agent needs exact artifact approval |
| AwaitingApproval | Executing | Yes, current approval and target checks pass |
| AwaitingApproval | ChatOnly | Yes, denied/timed-out approval returns advisory outcome |
| Executing | ToolCalling | Yes, ToolInvocationPolicy authorizes the call |
| Executing | Mutating ToolCalling | Only Agent mode plus approval/guard controls |
| ToolCalling | Validating | Yes, operation response received |
| Validating | Executing | Yes, applicable gates pass |
| Validating | Failed | Yes, record actual failure and count it |
| Failed | Planning | Only within configured count/time/failure controls; inject targeted failure context |
| Failed | Terminated | Finite work exhausted, cancellation or permanent failure; report cause. No product dollar exhaustion after migration. |
| Executing | Completed | All planned work/gates complete; actual effect evidence retained |
| Any | Executing by bypass | No, -32002; approval path remains mandatory |
Interim ACP defaults remain three planning rounds, 30 minutes and two repeated failures. Generic architecture diagrams do not override concrete configured execution limits. Independent evaluation budget exhaustion is a separate scoped stop, not product policy.

# 4A. Failure and retry lifecycle
Record the true failure, preserve receipts/effects and inject bounded failure context only when configured work limits permit another planning round. Keep count/time/repeated-failure controls distinct from provider attempts. The interim ACP defaults are three planning rounds, 30 minutes and two repeated failures. Product BudgetExhaustedError is retired by the accepted migration; independent evaluations may retain their scoped dollar stop.
The legacy host permits an initial attempt plus at most three retries. The inactive-policy Gateway separately permits at most three upstream attempts, including its legacy transient timeout/URL/5xx retries. Once enforcement is active, the Gateway permits one primary attempt and at most one identical-payload resend on the same route, only after a definitely NOT_SENT result (including a proven pre-connection timeout) or rejected HTTP 429. A timeout after connection, uncertain delivery, 5xx or unknown accounting is not resent. The host honors non-retryable classifications so it cannot multiply attempts. This resend policy adds no alternative-model recovery. ADR-029's single later recovery move is a separate interactive Auto planning action (§13.11), not a resend of an uncertain or failed provider attempt. The per-request timing budget is specified in §13.12. Each physical attempt retains its own receipt.

# 4B. Agent-mode directive plan and localized EDIT

These contracts are implemented at main `57e2069` (#407 / PR #411, with the merged #410 / PR #413 and #412 / PR #414 changes). Source paths in this section are under `src/optimus/`.

## 4B.1 Final plan and grammar

Every Agent-mode plan comes from the multi-turn planning loop (`agent/runner.py:476–495`). The final-plan directive set is READ, WRITE, EDIT and TEST. WRITE replaces the whole file from an opaque body (literal EDIT headers and marker lines remain content), fitting LF/CRLF body breaks to the existing file's uniform style (LF if it has no terminators), retaining its UTF-8 BOM, and replacing the body's last terminator according to the existing file's final-newline convention while preserving earlier empty lines (an empty body clears the text but retains an existing BOM); a new file uses LF and ends as the body does, and a mixed-ending target, including one with a lone CR, is refused unchanged as `WRITE_LINE_ENDINGS_MIXED` (`agent/tools.py:108–142`; `tools/mutation_tools.py:95–111`; `tools/line_endings.py:18–44`). MCP directives are invalid in a final plan.

A model emits EDIT without a base digest:

```text
EDIT <relative-path>
<<<<<<< OLD
<one or more OLD lines>
======= NEW
<zero or more NEW lines>
>>>>>>> END
```

Repeat the block for further changes to the same existing file. Each OLD contains at least one line; NEW may be empty to delete its OLD lines. Markers are whole lines compared after strip. They are reserved at directive positions and within EDIT parsing, with the WRITE-body exception above. A marker outside EDIT, out-of-order markers, an unterminated block, an empty OLD or zero blocks rejects the parse. Only CR, LF and CRLF end EDIT lines. Every non-EDIT plan uses the R1 `plan_lines` split: LF ends a line, CRLF stays paired, terminators are retained, and every other `str.splitlines()` separator is content. In that R1 split, `directive_text` prevents any line holding a content separator from becoming directive syntax. READ, WRITE, EDIT, TEST, MCP_LIST and MCP_CALL tokens use only spaces and tabs as separators and padding. If exact EDIT parsing did not return a valid EDIT, `_invents_an_edit` rejects an EDIT header visible only under `str.splitlines()` outside a WRITE body, even when that EDIT is malformed. One empty LF/CRLF line directly before the next recognized directive separates it from a WRITE body; other lines, including space-only lines, remain content. Planning-loop surface checks keep OLD/NEW bodies opaque and use R1 outside them (`agent/directives.py:10–25`, `:118–213`, `:265–305`, `:319–355`; `agent/planning_loop.py:633–649`).

The model must not supply `base_sha256` (`edit_base="forbidden"`). The harness rewrites only the header to `EDIT <relative-path> base_sha256=<64 lowercase hex>`. Re-parsing proves that nothing else changed (`agent/directives.py:244–276`; `agent/planning_loop.py:817–820`; `agent/runner.py:722–724`). Both prompt grammars document EDIT and the WRITE fitting/refusal rule under `AGENT_PLANNER_PROMPT_VERSION:2026-10-24-p407-edit-p410-write-line-endings` and `MULTI_TURN_PLANNER_PROMPT_VERSION:2026-10-24-p407-edit-p410-write-line-endings` (`agent/prompts.py:10–15`, `:40–50`).

## 4B.2 Evidence and binding before approval

The evidence digest is SHA-256 of the whole file's bytes when evidence was shown to the model. Turn-1 workspace context records it for each included file, whether shown whole or truncated (`agent/workspace_context.py:463–473`). A ranged READ records the whole-file `source_sha256` and `line_endings` from the same byte snapshot; its displayed READ_BLOCK header includes `eol=lf|crlf|mixed|none` (`loops/tools.py:112–130`; `agent/planning_loop.py:534–541`).

Only the final plan's turn counts. Initial-context digests are available only when that is planning turn 1, plus that turn's current reads (`agent/planning_loop.py:1951–1956`). The digest does not establish mechanical grounding of OLD; that remains #258.

`_finish_agent_planning` binds EDIT before calculating the plan hash. No evidence digest gives `EDIT_SOURCE_UNSEEN`; a changed file gives `EDIT_SOURCE_CHANGED`; a missing target with evidence gives `EDIT_TARGET_MISSING`. Binding failure occurs before the hash and approval. Approval text, plan hash and stored record use the bound text (`agent/runner.py:738–756`, `:1982–1994`). Approval shows the exact plan text, without an ACP diff.

## 4B.3 Apply and write

Fresh execution and stored-plan replay use the same sequence; replay never binds an EDIT (`agent/runner.py:1470–1536`):

1. Refuse an unbound EDIT with `EDIT_SOURCE_UNSEEN`.
2. Refuse a target that is not a file with `EDIT_TARGET_MISSING`.
3. Perform a gated raw read with `newline=""`. A decode error gives `EDIT_NOT_UTF8`.
4. Compare the base digest. A mismatch gives `EDIT_SOURCE_CHANGED`.
5. Run `apply_edit_blocks` against the base.
6. Perform the exact gated write through `AgentToolbox.write_file`, which forwards EDIT's `newline=""` and `expected_sha256` to `write_file` rather than the WRITE fitting adapter. The shared `_authorize_file_mutation` runs `assert_mutation_allowed(WRITE_FILE)` / `MutationGuard`, then `PreToolGuard` with `FILE_WRITE` and `generation_scope=FILE_MUTATION`. After the guard allows it, re-hash the target bytes immediately before writing. A mismatch raises `WriteSourceChanged`, a `MutationForbidden`, and gives `EDIT_SOURCE_CHANGED`. The write uses `write_text(encoding="utf-8", newline="")` (`agent/tools.py:104–147`; `tools/mutation_tools.py:67–92`, `:114–140`; `runtime/mutation.py:40–41`). The exact `write_file` primitive now defaults to `newline=""` for every caller.

This is a direct working-tree write after exact approval and guards. The ACP WRITE/EDIT path uses no diff parser, `ShadowWorkspaceMutationRunner`, shadow apply, rollback or pre-write fitness check. The shadow runner is constructed only in `retry/gated_run.py:103`; no production path constructs `GatedRetryRunner`. Plan TESTs run afterwards in the working tree (`agent/runner.py:869–907`, `:1190–1225`). The sequence is not atomic against concurrent external writers.

## 4B.4 Matching and byte preservation

`apply_edit_blocks` matches OLD whole lines exactly once, excluding terminators. Blocks must not overlap and are applied to the base, not successively to earlier replacement results. Only CR, LF and CRLF end a line (`agent/edits.py:55–110`).

A leading BOM is excluded from OLD matching and kept, unless every line is deleted, which leaves zero bytes. NEW lines use the first matched line's terminator, or LF when it has none. The last NEW line keeps the last matched line's terminator. Deleting trailing lines keeps the newly exposed line's existing terminator. Bytes outside matched lines are unchanged.

## 4B.5 Typed failure and lifecycle

The closed applicability codes are `EDIT_TARGET_MISSING`, `EDIT_NOT_UTF8`, `EDIT_SOURCE_UNSEEN`, `EDIT_SOURCE_CHANGED`, `EDIT_OLD_NOT_FOUND`, `EDIT_OLD_NOT_UNIQUE` and `EDIT_BLOCKS_OVERLAP` (`agent/edits.py:15–25`). An applicability failure ends the run with status FAILED and internal stop reason `EDIT_NOT_APPLICABLE`. At main `31c6de5` (#576) the ACP prompt response for that turn has wire `stopReason` `end_turn`, not `refusal`, and `_meta` `{"runStopReason": "EDIT_NOT_APPLICABLE", "outcome": "failed"}` (#559 / PR #569; #268 / PR #561; `acp/spec.py:4135`, `:4278–4308`). This holds for a binding failure before approval and for an applicability failure after it. If a cancel was accepted first, `_meta.outcome` is `cancelled` instead, and before approval `stopReason` is `cancelled` too (`acp/spec.py:2514–2526`; `acp/lifecycle.py:337–341`). The stopped run's text is never sent as a plan: a binding failure sends no plan update, and after approval no completed-plan update is sent, because only a COMPLETED run sends one (#570 / PR #630; `acp/spec.py:3967–3969`, `:4019–4028`).

The completion text is one fixed message per code, built only from the code and the path the plan named, never file content (#574; `agent/edits.py:28–52`, `:66–76`). It is a single line, wrapped here:

```text
The change was not made to <path>, because <reason>.
The plan made no changes and ran none of its tests. <next step>. (<code>)
```

Each code has its own `<reason>` and `<next step>`. For example, `EDIT_OLD_NOT_FOUND` gives "the lines it replaces are not in the file exactly as planned" and "Send your request again to get a new plan".

During execution, the plan's WRITE terminal is `suppressed`, or `failed_no_effect` after the post-guard digest re-check. Every plan TEST is `suppressed` (`agent/runner.py:1482–1526`, `:1547–1552`). Binding failures occur before approval. Applicability failure stops the run; it does not enter fitness-driven replanning. Ordinary guard, I/O and cancellation failures keep their existing effect classification (`agent/runner.py:203–234`). Completion text is passed through by `_completion_message` (`acp/spec.py:4141–4142` at `31c6de5`).

## 4B.6 Logging and persistence

Typed applicability failures and successful application are offered to the opt-in ACP debug trace at `runner.py:edit`, hypothesis `P407-EDIT`. Digests are populated where available: a failure has no result digest, and a binding failure has no base digest. These EDIT debug records contain no file or model content (`agent/runner.py:2002–2012`).

`AgentRunResult.edit_failure_code` is set by `_edit_failure_result` to the specific closed `EDIT_*` applicability code for an `EDIT_NOT_APPLICABLE` run; it is `None` for other runner results. The seven-code vocabulary is enforced by the producing failure paths, not by the field's `str | None` type (`agent/models.py:175–177`; `agent/runner.py:1615–1639`; `agent/edits.py:15–52`).

Always-on `agent_run` telemetry now carries that code in the always-present nullable `edit_failure_code` key beside `stop_reason`; ordinary composition attempts to append it to `.optimus/telemetry.jsonl` (#412 / PR #414). This key carries no path, file or model content. Persistence is attempted, not guaranteed: sink errors are contained. After transport abandonment, ordinary `agent_run` emission is suppressed and no such persistence is attempted (`agent/runner.py:356–361`, `:1320–1350`; `telemetry/events.py:568–611`; `acp/bootstrap.py:129–156`; `telemetry/jsonl.py:34–43`; `telemetry/fanout.py:108–123`).

The ACP `agent/run` result payload also includes `edit_failure_code` because the dispatcher serializes the whole result model; this response field is not itself durable persistence (`acp/dispatcher.py:376–382`). Completion text still carries the code into transient conversation history, and the opt-in EDIT trace still carries it (`acp/spec.py:1589–1597`, `:2121–2122`; `agent/runner.py:2002–2012`). The code is not stored in Redis run metadata or the plan record: the Redis sink maps selected metadata fields and `AgentPlanRecord` has no such field (`telemetry/redis_sink.py:70–86`; `telemetry/redis_adapter.py:30–36`, `:134–146`; `agent/state_store.py:89–114`).

## 4B.7 Retained limits and ownership

| Limit | Owning issue or retained contract |
|---|---|
| At most one declared WRITE/EDIT target; multi-target mutation directives cannot be expressed. This does not confine TEST subprocess effects | #408 |
| Locating the target lines in large files | #409 |
| Mechanical grounding of OLD | #258 |
| No atomicity against external writers | #407 / PR #411 execution contract; `agent/runner.py`, `tools/mutation_tools.py` |
| Exact plan-text approval, without an ACP diff | #407 / PR #411 approval contract; `agent/runner.py` |
| WRITE remains a whole-file replacement, with line-ending/BOM/last-line fitting and mixed-ending refusal implemented at this pin; it does not use EDIT's localized byte-preservation contract | #410 / PR #413 implemented contract; `agent/directives.py`, `agent/tools.py`, `tools/line_endings.py`, `tools/mutation_tools.py` (§4B.1) |

A mixed-ending WRITE raises `WriteRefused` before writing, settles WRITE as `failed_no_effect`, ends the run FAILED with `WRITE_LINE_ENDINGS_MIXED`, and suppresses every plan TEST; ACP forwards the refusal text and reports wire `stopReason=end_turn` (`agent/runner.py:203–234`, `:1272–1297`, `:1455–1465`; `acp/spec.py:2123–2124`, `:2212–2221`). The refusal speaks only for that WRITE and its subsequent TESTs, not earlier planning-turn effects.

The guarded write declares `FILE_MUTATION` for WRITE and EDIT alike; EDIT is not assigned `PATCH_PROPOSAL`. Section 14 records the unit/runner, full-suite, CI and bounded live evidence with their original pins.

# 5. ADL parser continuity and architectural evolution
ADLParserStrategy retains parse_and_validate(adl_rules: list[str], proposed_diff: str) -> tuple[bool, list[dict]] as its abstract validation contract. PrototypeRegexADLParser retains the existing ASSERT(<a>) HAS NO DEPENDENCY ON <b> matching grammar, lowercases captured names for code import checks, and checks both an import <b> occurrence and the org.springframework.<b> substring in the diff. Violations retain rule, Structural Pollution metric and Violation: (<a> -> <b>) value. It returns true only when the violations list is empty. The regex implementation is a prototype and does not become a new semantic analyzer through this migration.

# 9C.1 Deterministic search contract (target) and the implemented provider

**Implemented at 91fd64a:** the Gateway's `/v1/tools/web/search` route is served by `TavilyWebToolProvider` (`optimus_gateway/tool_providers.py`), configured with the Gateway-only `TAVILY_API_KEY`; its usage is recorded as provider-native `tavily_credits`. The contract below is the accepted target for replacing that provider with a dedicated aggregator request; it is not implemented in the Gateway.

The target converts an authorized search request into a dedicated OpenRouter Chat Completions request using one cheap Flash/Haiku-class model, low `max_tokens`, and `plugins: [{"id": "web"}]`. Search is never attached to the primary generation call.

```text
{
  "model": "google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "<minimal search request>"}],
  "max_tokens": 16,
  "plugins": [{
    "id": "web",
    "max_results": 3,
    "search_prompt": "<policy-bounded query>"
  }]
}
```

The Gateway would forward the effective domain policy, parse only `annotations[].url_citation`, independently revalidate every returned URL, and copy upstream usage/cost. Assistant prose and annotation character offsets are not evidence.

## Measured baseline (architecture spike, 2026-07-27)

| Measurement | Value | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Minimal-call annotations present | 3/3 | `tools/run_openrouter_web_search_spike.py`, run against OpenRouter directly |
| Include-domain violations | 0 | same spike |
| Exclude-domain violations | 0 | same spike |
| Citations structurally complete | 9/9 | same spike |
| Mean latency per search | 7,068.7 ms | same spike; one host, one day |
| Mean reported cost | $0.0051584 | same spike; prices of that day |

These values were produced by the spike tool, not by a Gateway test, and the spike is an experimental measurement harness, not production Gateway code. Three to five sequential searches would project to 21.2-35.3 seconds at that latency. The supplied Tavily comparison (about 1-2 seconds and $0.008/search) was not measured in this spike. The deterministic aggregator plugin is deprecated by OpenRouter (§9C.2), so the target itself is conditional.
